column2: It is a grave thing to ask the Grand Judge [court_judge.GetTitledFirstName] to part me from my husband [Root.Spouse.GetTitledFirstName]. The Sacred Law of Ormazd allows it, but the whole court will know, and there is no taking it back. I must be certain this is what I want.
I have decided.
I cannot decide this now...
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] asks the Grand Judge [This.GetTitledFirstName] for a divorce

[From.GetTitledFirstName] came before me to ask for a divorce from [From.GetHerHis] husband [From.Spouse.GetTitledFirstName]. I reminded [From.GetHerHim] of the iddah, the month of waiting before a divorce is sealed, and asked many questions about the marriage. Now the Law waits on my word.
If you have no regrets after a month, you may be divorced.
No. I see no cause to grant you a divorce.
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] grants [This.GetTitledFirstName] the divorce [This.GetSheHe] asked for
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] refuses [This.GetTitledFirstName] the divorce

The Grand Judge [From.GetTitledFirstName] asked what I would do if my husband [Root.Spouse.GetTitledFirstName] demanded the mahr back, the bride-gift he gave me at our wedding, and told me what would become of any child of our union. Then [From.GetSheHe] granted the divorce, to be sealed once the iddah has passed.
A month I must wait, then.
Not until this child is born, then.
I have changed my mind. I do not want the divorce!
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] decides to stay with [This.GetTitledFirstName]
The Grand Judge [From.GetTitledFirstName] would not grant me a divorce. From all I told [From.GetHerHim], [From.GetSheHe] saw no reason in the Law to part me from [Root.Spouse.GetTitledFirstName].
Then I must bear this marriage.
The iddah has passed. If I am truly certain I want to be free of [Root.Spouse.GetTitledFirstName], one word from me seals it.
It is done. I am no longer married!
In this month I have changed my mind. I will stay.

My wife [divorcing_wife.GetTitledFirstName] has gone behind my back to the Grand Judge [From.GetTitledFirstName] and asked for a divorce! If she still wants it when the iddah has passed, our marriage is over...
If that is what she wants...
NO! I will not allow it!
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] rides after [This.GetTitledFirstName] to make [This.GetHerHim] reconsider

I was on my way home, wondering how to tell my husband [From.GetTitledFirstName] what I had done, when [From.GetSheHe] caught up with me on the road and demanded to know why I wanted a divorce. So I told [From.GetHerHim]. All of it.
I do not want to be married to you. I want that divorce!
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] will not change [Root.GetHerHis] mind about the divorce
Fine, I will stay. But things are going to change!

I pleaded with [From.GetTitledFirstName] and promised her anything if only she would not leave me. She told me her reasons, and I swore by the Flame of Truth that I would change, that I would do anything, anything!
But [From.GetTitledFirstName] did not change her mind.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] promised not to leave me!

I grow more worried by the day. No Grand Judge has been chosen, and it is as if [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] does not care whether the Sacred Law of Ormazd is kept in this realm at all! Someone must speak up.

The Grand Judge [old_judge.GetTitledFirstName] is a disgrace. [old_judge.GetSheHeCap] barely knows the Law, sleeps through the hearings and hands down verdicts as if casting knucklebones. As long as [old_judge.GetSheHe] holds the post there will be no justice under [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName].
One of the courtiers would serve far better!
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] puts forward a candidate for Grand Judge to [This.GetTitledFirstName]
Why, I would make the best Grand Judge!
One of [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]'s vassals is the right choice.
Hold my tongue. [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] knows best.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] came to me, worried that my realm has no Grand Judge to keep the Sacred Law, and put forward [target_suggested_qadi.GetTitledFirstName] for the post.

Fuming at what [From.GetSheHe] called 'another disastrous verdict of your Grand Judge', [From.GetTitledFirstName] begged me to throw out [old_judge.GetTitledFirstName] and give the post to [target_suggested_qadi.GetTitledFirstName] instead.
Yes. [target_suggested_qadi.GetTitledFirstName] shall be my Grand Judge.
The old Grand Judge, [This.GetTitledFirstName], is dismissed
[This.GetTitledFirstName] is made Grand Judge
[This.GetTitledFirstName] is made Grand Judge
No. I see no reason for it.
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] refuses to make [This.GetTitledFirstName] Grand Judge
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] dismisses [This.GetTitledFirstName]'s candidate

I had no idea [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] would put my name forward! The letter appointing me Grand Judge to [From.GetTitledFirstName], with an order to come before [From.GetHerHim] at once, left me quite bewildered.
My thanks, [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]!
The new Grand Judge, [Root.GetTitledFirstName], thanks [This.GetTitledFirstName]
I put forward [target_suggested_qadi.GetTitledFirstName] as Grand Judge, and waited with bated breath while [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] weighed my counsel.

The Grand Judge was such a disgrace, with arbitrary verdicts and no grasp of the Law, that I had to name someone better. [target_suggested_qadi.GetTitledFirstName] is learned and diligent, and I waited with bated breath while [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] weighed my counsel.
[Root.Liege.GetSheHeCap] appointed my candidate! Praise the One!
I was sent away and told not to meddle again.
It felt presumptuous, even shameless, to put myself forward as Grand Judge to [From.GetTitledFirstName]. But I could think of no better candidate than myself.

I insulted the old Grand Judge to [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s face when I said I knew the Law far better and would judge far more wisely. But I saw no other way to be rid of the fool, and it was [From.GetTitledFirstName] who would judge between us.
I am the new Grand Judge! Fear my justice!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] did not want me as Grand Judge.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has stripped me of the post of Grand Judge, all on the word of [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName], who whispered that I am arbitrary and ignorant of the Law! Years of service, thrown away on a courtier's spite.
May the One burn [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]'s house to ash!

The Scriptures of the Prophets say: 'Wine and games of chance, and offerings to stones, are the filth of the Great Conspirator. Shun them, that you may prosper.' And it is said that the Prophet al-Quyat had drunkards beaten with palm stalks and sandals. [target_drunkard.GetTitledFirstName] reeks of wine again, and the whole court has smelled it.
Eighty lashes for that drunkard!
[This.GetTitledFirstName] is given eighty lashes by the Grand Judge [Root.GetTitledFirstName]
Show mercy. Let the drunkard repent.
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] spares the drunkard [This.GetTitledFirstName] the eighty lashes
It is not worth the trouble.

I stumbled into the Grand Judge [From.GetTitledFirstName], who smelled the wine on my breath and had me seized on the spot. The next morning I was tied to a post in the courtyard and given my eighty lashes.
The lashes made me howl, but the wine will take the pain away...
I will never drink again, as the One is my witness!

The wine flowed, and when I left my friends I could barely stand. I woke up in the Grand Judge [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s chambers with a split head, to be told that a small gift to the poor and a promise to drink no more would spare me the lash.
I promised, but all I could think of was a jug of wine for my head.
As the One is my witness, I will never drink again!

The court is buzzing with rumours that [unfaithful_vassal.GetTitledFirstName], a vassal of [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], is lying with a woman who is not his wife. No true follower of the One would commit zina!
The Grand Judge will know what to do.
The Grand Judge [This.GetTitledFirstName] hears that [unfaithful_vassal.GetTitledFirstName] keeps a lover
I will confront him myself and make him repent before the One!
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] confronts [This.GetTitledFirstName] about his lover
It is not for me to judge others.

To accuse anyone of zina, of lying with someone not their spouse, is no light thing. [From.GetTitledFirstName] has told me of the rumours at [From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]'s court about [unfaithful_vassal.GetTitledFirstName] and a woman he is far too friendly with...
I will confront the accused.
[This.GetTitledFirstName] is accused of zina and confronted by the Grand Judge [Root.GetTitledFirstName]
If you care so much, confront him yourself!
The Grand Judge [Root.GetTitledFirstName] will not act on [This.GetTitledFirstName]'s accusation
Do not come to me with rumours!

The days with my lover have been the happiest of my life. Now [From.GetTitledFirstName] threatens to take the whole affair to the Grand Judge, and all that joy feels small and soiled. Zina is a sin, but I could not resist her...
Bribe [From.GetTitledFirstName] to keep quiet.
[Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s gold is offered to buy [This.GetTitledFirstName]'s silence
I promise I will never see her again!
[Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s promise may satisfy [This.GetTitledFirstName]
Our love is sacred, whatever the Scriptures say!
[This.GetTitledFirstName] may take the matter to the Grand Judge
The Grand Judge [From.GetTitledFirstName] lectured me at length on the sin of zina. All I could think of was my beloved, waiting for me in our little hideaway.
You have no witnesses, only rumours, and they are lies!
[This.GetTitledFirstName] may be convinced of [Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s innocence
[This.GetTitledFirstName] may doubt [Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s denials
I confess, and I will end it.
[This.GetTitledFirstName] will weigh [Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s confession and promise
I deny nothing, and I will do nothing about it!
[This.GetTitledFirstName] will find a fitting punishment for [Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s sins

The Grand Judge [From.GetTitledFirstName] questioned me at length about the rumours, what I had heard and from whom, and what I thought of [unfaithful_vassal.GetTitledFirstName]. It was rather flattering. Then [From.GetSheHe] gave me [From.GetHerHis] answer.
[From.GetSheHeCap] will do nothing at all!
I may confront the sinner, but without [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s help.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] swore the sinner would be punished.
I had not expected [From.GetTitledFirstName] to take my threat of the Grand Judge quite like this...
Greed won. I took the gold and will say nothing to anyone.
I spit on your gold! The Grand Judge will hear of this.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] laughed at me! Off to the Grand Judge.
The Grand Judge would not believe me anyway.
A promise is not enough. The Grand Judge will hear of this.
[From.GetTitledFirstName]'s promise is enough for me.

I put [court_accuser.GetTitledFirstName]'s accusation to [From.GetTitledFirstName], and the rumours behind it. [From.GetSheHeCap] denied everything and swore [From.GetSheHe] is a pious servant of the One who would never so offend the Flame of Truth.
I believe [From.GetTitledFirstName].
The Grand Judge [Root.GetTitledFirstName] believes [This.GetTitledFirstName] is innocent
I doubt [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s word, but I have no witnesses.
The Grand Judge [Root.GetTitledFirstName] doubts [This.GetTitledFirstName]'s word but lets [This.GetHerHim] go
I need no witnesses nor confessions. [From.GetTitledFirstName] will be punished!
The Law asks for stoning for zina, but the Grand Judge settles for a hundred lashes

An accusation of zina is not to be taken lightly. Yet when I confronted [From.GetTitledFirstName], [From.GetSheHe] confessed, four times as the Law demands, and swore never to see [From.GetHerHis] lover again. Should I punish [From.GetHerHim], or be merciful?
I do not believe you, but there is nothing I can do.
Your words are hollow. You and your lover will both be lashed!
Break that promise and you get two hundred lashes!
The merciful Grand Judge [Root.GetTitledFirstName] trusts [This.GetTitledFirstName]'s word

I had expected some shame, some remorse, from [From.GetTitledFirstName] for committing zina, a sin the Scriptures of the Prophets punish with stoning or a hundred lashes. Instead [From.GetSheHe] denied nothing and told me the love [From.GetSheHe] feels for [From.GetHerHis] lover is sacred!
I... I do not know what to do...
The Grand Judge does not know what to do, and [This.GetTitledFirstName] escapes punishment
A hundred lashes, then!

The Scriptures of the Prophets call zina a crime, to be punished by stoning or a hundred lashes. Whatever I told the Grand Judge [From.GetTitledFirstName], I was afraid as [From.GetSheHe] weighed my case.
The lashes cut my back, but not my soul nor my love!
The merciful Grand Judge [From.GetTitledFirstName] spared me the lash!
I will never see my lover again, and [From.GetTitledFirstName] spared me.

I mean to cover the walls of my temple of the One with the verses of the Scriptures of the Prophets, in flowing script and endless arabesques. Such work is beyond any local scribe, but my liege's Court Calligrapher, [court_calligrapher.GetTitledFirstName], could do it.
With [court_calligrapher.GetTitledFirstName]'s hand, the temple will be wonderful!
The Court Calligrapher [This.GetTitledFirstName] is asked to design the inscriptions of the temple
I should not trouble the Court Calligrapher with such a petty task.
A letter from [From.GetTitledFirstName] has arrived, most respectful in tone, humbly asking me to design the inscriptions of the Scriptures of the Prophets for [From.GetHerHis] temple.
I would be honoured to design them.
[This.GetTitledFirstName] is delighted with the designs
Despite [Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s labours, [This.GetTitledFirstName] does not think much of the designs
My work would be wasted on such a petty temple.
The Court Calligrapher [Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s refusal bitterly disappoints [This.GetTitledFirstName]
Samples have come from the Court Calligrapher [From.GetTitledFirstName]: the inscriptions for my temple, with special care given to the verses I most wanted on its dome and walls.
[From.GetSheHeCap] has outdone [From.GetHerselfHimself]! Bravo, [From.GetTitledFirstName]!
The Court Calligrapher [This.GetTitledFirstName] hears the work is praised
Word of the Court Calligrapher's fine work reaches [This.GetTitledFirstName]
It looks as if a three-year-old smeared ink across the parchment!
The Court Calligrapher [This.GetTitledFirstName] hears the work is found wanting
Word of the Court Calligrapher's poor designs reaches [This.GetTitledFirstName]
The designs are good, but [From.GetTitledFirstName] can do better.
The designs are awful, but I cannot tell [From.GetTitledFirstName] that!

I had thought it a great honour for [From.GetTitledFirstName] to design the inscriptions of my temple. I even sent [From.GetHerHim] the verses I wanted, with a humble letter praising [From.GetHerHis] hand. The answer was humiliating in its brevity.
'No' was all it said.

I sent [From.GetTitledFirstName] samples of my earlier work and the verses [From.GetSheHe] had asked for, set out in my finest hand. Now the messenger is back with [From.GetHerHis] answer, and I tear the seal...
[From.GetSheHeCap] loved it! Now the real work begins!
[From.GetSheHeCap] thought the designs were dreadful!
[From.GetSheHeCap] chided me for not taking this seriously!
[From.GetSheHeCap] was happy with the designs.

I have seen the inscriptions my Court Calligrapher [court_calligrapher.GetTitledFirstName] designed for [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s temple. I cannot believe anyone would be unhappy with them. [court_calligrapher.GetTitledFirstName] is a master of the reed pen!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] was most pleased with them.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] did not share my opinion...
[From.GetTitledFirstName] found fault after fault and called them unworthy.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] agreed with me and praised [court_calligrapher.GetTitledFirstName] to the skies.

The hilya I have laboured over for so long is finished: the word-portrait of the Prophet al-Quyat, his face and bearing and character, written in gold leaf with as much care given to every curve and dot as my hand could give. The colours blaze, and the detail is a joy to behold.
I shall send it to the Calif!
The Calif [This.GetTitledFirstName] is sent the hilya
I shall honour my liege [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] with it.
[Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s liege [This.GetTitledFirstName] is sent the hilya
I shall sell it, and make another with the gold.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has sent me a hilya of [From.GetHerHis] own making, the word-portrait of the Prophet al-Quyat written in gold on parchment, with the prayer that it guard me from harm in this world and the next.
Beautiful! My thanks, [From.GetTitledFirstName].
Accept this small token of my thanks.
Did I ask for this? I have hilyas far finer than this one!

A Scripture of the Prophets with gilded margins and a cover of solid gold: only the greatest calligraphers could make such a thing. If I promise one to my liege [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], [Root.Liege.GetSheHe] might well part with a great deal of gold for the 'materials'...
Ask [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] to pay for the whole book.
[This.GetTitledFirstName] is asked to pay for all the gold of the Golden Scripture
Ask [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] to pay for part of it.
[This.GetTitledFirstName] is asked to help pay for the gold of the Golden Scripture
My dream will remain a dream...

A Golden Scripture sounds absurd, and the gold alone would cost a fortune. Still, I listened patiently as my Court Calligrapher [From.GetTitledFirstName] laid out [From.GetHerHis] plans, the cost of the gold and the vellum and the six months the work would take. It began to sound like something worthy of my court. Then [From.GetTitledFirstName] asked me...
To pay for all of it? Yes, of course!
To pay for some of it? As long as that is all.
No. A 'Golden Scripture', how absurd!
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] pays [This.GetTitledFirstName] for the Golden Scripture
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] refuses to pay for the Golden Scripture
With a rough reckoning of the cost of the gold and a promise of six months' work, I had [From.GetTitledFirstName] hanging on my every word about my 'dream' of a Golden Scripture...
[From.GetTitledFirstName] agreed to pay for everything I might need!
It worked. [From.GetTitledFirstName] will pay for some of the 'materials'!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] refused to pay for 'something so foolish'!

Six months ago I agreed to pay for my Court Calligrapher [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s Golden Scripture. I have heard no word of progress, nor seen so much as a gilded page, and my spies say the gold went on silks and a new house. I have been swindled!
Throw [From.GetTitledFirstName] into the dungeon.
Banish [From.GetTitledFirstName] from my court.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] will pay back every coin.
Let it go. It is only gold.

The Golden Scripture I promised [From.GetTitledFirstName] was never more than a fancy, a scheme to part my liege from some gold. Somehow [From.GetTitledFirstName] has found out, and I have lost my post. And now...
...I am thrown into [From.GetHerHis] dungeon!
...I am banished from [From.GetHerHis] court!
...I must pay back every coin!
The ghazal, with its pain of parting and its beauty of love in spite of that pain, is the perfect form for my next song. The verses have come at last, and the oud is tuned.
My new ballad is finished at last: a song of love lost and love endured, of longing across the miles. It is the best thing I have ever written, and it deserves the right ears.
I will sing it for [Root.Liege.Spouse.GetTitledFirstName].
The Court Musician [Root.GetTitledFirstName] sings the new song for [Root.GetHerHis] liege's wife [This.GetTitledFirstName]
[Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] shall be the first to hear it!
The Court Musician [Root.GetTitledFirstName] sings the new song for [This.GetTitledFirstName]
I need more time to master it.

My husband's Court Musician [From.GetTitledFirstName] has a wonderful voice, and I could barely keep from blushing as [From.GetSheHe] sang me a ghazal of the pain of parting and the beauty of love in spite of it...

My husband's Court Musician [From.GetTitledFirstName] has a wonderful voice, and I could barely keep from blushing as [From.GetSheHe] sang me a ballad of longing and love, looking at me the whole time...
Wonderful! Our court would be poorer without your voice.
[Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s delight in the song gladdens [This.GetTitledFirstName]
It is not proper to court a married woman so!
[Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s husband [This.GetTitledFirstName] hears that the Court Musician sang to [Root.GetHerHim]

The Court Musician [court_musician.GetTitledFirstName] sang [court_musician.GetHerHis] new song for me, and [court_musician.GetSheHe] did it justice: the pain of parting and the beauty of love in spite of it, in a voice that silenced the whole hall.

My wife [From.GetTitledFirstName] tells me that my Court Musician [court_musician.GetTitledFirstName] sang her a love song, gazing at her all the while. A ghazal, a ballad, call it what you like: it was sung to my wife.
Here is a small token from [From.GetTitledFirstName] and me.
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] and [Root.Spouse.GetTitledFirstName] reward the Court Musician [This.GetTitledFirstName]
How dare you court my wife with a song!? Seize [court_musician.GetHerHim]!
The Court Musician [This.GetTitledFirstName] is imprisoned for courting [Root.Spouse.GetTitledFirstName]
Play it once more, please?
As I sang I felt the pain of parting from my own love, and still saw the beauty of love itself. It was my masterpiece, and as the last notes died away I found tears running down my face...
[From.GetTitledFirstName] was as moved by the song as I was.
Both [From.GetTitledFirstName] and [From.Spouse.GetTitledFirstName] loved my song.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] did not like me singing to [From.GetHerHis] wife!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] wept and called for the song again and again.

'Through my veins both love and blood flow
My beloved fills me as love empties me of myself...'

I am stuck on the next line. I have walked the gardens all morning, looking for something, anything, to set the words free...
I find it in [Root.Liege.Spouse.GetTitledFirstName], and recite the poem to her.
The Court Poet [Root.GetTitledFirstName] recites [Root.GetHerHis] poem to [This.GetTitledFirstName]
The garden inspires me. I present the poem to [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName].
The Court Poet [Root.GetTitledFirstName] presents [Root.GetHerHis] poem to [This.GetTitledFirstName]
No inspiration comes. The poem stays unfinished...

My husband's garden is an easy place to dream in, and I was walking slowly through it when the Court Poet [From.GetTitledFirstName] startled me. [From.GetSheHeCap] begged my pardon and recited a poem [From.GetSheHe] said had come to [From.GetHerHim] the moment [From.GetSheHe] saw me.
Hardly proper, but very sweet.
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] has only kind words for the Court Poet [This.GetTitledFirstName]'s poem
Go away! What will my husband say?!
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] tells [Root.GetHerHis] husband [This.GetTitledFirstName] about the Court Poet's poem

The poem did not rhyme. Why did it not rhyme? Should poems not rhyme? The Court Poet [court_poet.GetTitledFirstName] assured me that not all poetry does, and I did like the first two lines:

'Through my veins both love and blood flow
My beloved fills me as love empties me of myself...'

My wife [From.GetTitledFirstName] came to me flushed and flustered. The Court Poet [court_poet.GetTitledFirstName] had found her alone in my garden and recited her a poem about love and blood and beloveds. It did not even rhyme.
Good work, my poet, good work.
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] pays the Court Poet [This.GetTitledFirstName] for a copy of the poem
Did you mean to seduce my wife with this?! Seize [court_poet.GetHerHim]!
The Court Poet [This.GetTitledFirstName] is imprisoned for wooing [Root.Spouse.GetTitledFirstName]
The most beautiful poem I have ever heard!

My new poem is the talk of the court. People ask me for copies, or to recite it just once more. I try to be discreet about it. I would rather no jealous husband or wife came after me over a few sweet verses...
It seems [From.GetTitledFirstName] liked it...
[From.GetTitledFirstName] even paid me for a copy!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] did not like me finding inspiration in [From.GetHerHis] wife...
[From.GetTitledFirstName] was moved to tears by my poem.

As Cupbearer I serve the wine at [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]'s table and guard [Root.Liege.GetHerHis] cup against poison, sometimes tasting it myself. A shame I cannot stand my liege. It would be so easy to pour from the wrong flask...
Poison the wine [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] will drink.
The poison is discovered before any harm is done
I dare not risk my place at [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]'s court.

My trusted servant [From.GetTitledFirstName] served me as always, and though it tasted strange I thought nothing of it until it was too late! I have been poisoned, why else would I feel like this? And my spies have found who did it.

Something in what [From.GetTitledFirstName] set before me tonight smelled wrong. A morsel fed to a hound, and the beast was dead before it hit the floor. Poison! [From.GetSheHeCap] has served at my table for years, and all that time [From.GetSheHe] wished me dead.
Imprison that [From.GetManWoman]! OBEY MY VOICE!
[This.GetTitledFirstName] is imprisoned by the raving [Root.GetTitledFirstName]
Into the dungeon with the traitor!
The poisoner [This.GetTitledFirstName] is imprisoned before the poison can do harm
Count yourself lucky I only imprison you. You should be dead!
[Root.GetTitledFirstName] imprisons [This.GetTitledFirstName], though [Root.GetSheHe] would rather see [This.GetHerHim] dead
For the poisoner is death! I mean, kill [From.GetHerHim]!
For your treason you will die!
I would kill you myself if I had the strength!
My treason reached the wrong ears! Why did I trust the poison to kill [From.GetTitledFirstName]? I should have done it with my own two hands!

My plan was to dose myself until no poison could touch me and let the poisoned dish pass. It did not work out. I missed the poison meant for [From.GetTitledFirstName], and that is how I ended up in [From.GetHerHis] dungeon...
At least the bastard is as sick as a dog!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] did not even get sick!
The poison drove [From.GetHerHim] mad, at least...

Food Taster to [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] is a dangerous post. I taste every dish and every cup before [Root.Liege.GetSheHe] does, to make sure none is poisoned. Lately I have been dosing myself with small sips of poison, to grow immune, for fear of death has its claws in me. And if I am immune, I might let a poisoned dish pass...
If [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] dies because I am immune, all the better!
It is my duty to keep my liege safe. I will stop this madness.

I have looked over the plans for the buildings going up in [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName]'s realm, and they chill my blood. So many faults, so many small flaws that could be mended, if only [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] would listen to me and pay for the work.
[Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] must approve these changes!
The Chief Architect [Root.GetTitledFirstName] asks [This.GetTitledFirstName] for gold to mend the building plans
I need more time. There are surely more flaws to find...

'You see, this small change means five more years without repairs, and this, this is simply absurd, what were they thinking?
